key_points: Initial request (SH-REQ): deploy an AI agent to auto-fix rejected shipment notices and blanket-resubmit them (scenario.initial_request, CL-01).

Problem as finally defined (PD-1): ORG-A shipment notices are rejected by carrier ORG-B due to carrier-side business-rule checks for LOC_UNKNOWN (x2) and EVENT_ORDER (x1), not generic content errors or carrier-system flakiness; handoff H-1 is HEALTHY/VALID (E-01, F-01).

Established via reject-log evidence E-01 (3 records: N-1 LOC_UNKNOWN, N-2 LOC_UNKNOWN, N-3 EVENT_ORDER); this contradicted the requester's own content-error framing (CL-01 status CONTRADICTED, H-CONTENT-ERRORS REJECTED) and the later 'carrier is flaky' claim (CL-02/E-02, UNVERIFIED, H-CARRIER-SYSTEM-FLAKY still CANDIDATE).

DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two HIGH-criticality unknowns (sample representativeness, upstream-vs-carrier origin) into open verification obligations VOB-U-SMALL-SAMPLE-SIZE and VOB-U-UPSTREAM-VS-CARRIER-ORIGIN.
What was released: only the diagnostic deliverable (diagnose_reject_reasons on DA-REJ, work item W-WI-1, DONE) within SD-1's release_scope; this confirms LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER as reject drivers.

What was NOT released: correction of location/sequence data in ORG-A's process P-1 and resubmission via handoff H-1, both part of PD-1's intended_scope but outside the actual release_scope and blocked by the two open VOBs.

Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with an empty hold list, meaning the diagnostic scope that was released is released as-is, while unresolved items are documented as limitations rather than withheld.

Two root-cause-removing remedies (pre-submission validation in P-1; carrier reference-data sync) are marked not feasible in contest time and remain unfinished; a third remedy (expanding the reject-log sample) is feasible but explicitly does not remove the root cause.
limitations_explained: The diagnosis rests on only 3 observed reject records, and the reject log's completeness is of unknown status, so this sample may not represent the full reject population (VOB-U-SMALL-SAMPLE-SIZE, open, HIGH impact).

It is still unresolved whether the LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER mismatches originate from a gap in ORG-A's own process (P-1) or from stale/incomplete reference data held by carrier ORG-B (VOB-U-UPSTREAM-VS-CARRIER-ORIGIN, open, HIGH impact); correction work is blocked on this.
Releasing the diagnosis does not by itself reduce the reject rate: the only feasible-in-time remedy (expanding the reject-log sample) is explicitly marked removes_root_cause: false.

The two remedies that would actually remove the root cause - adding pre-submission validation in ORG-A's P-1, and establishing a cross-org reference-data sync agreement with ORG-B - are both marked not feasible in the available time and remain unfinished.

Correcting and resubmitting shipment notices cannot proceed until both open VOBs are resolved, and the reference-data-sync remedy additionally requires cross-org authorization between ORG-A and ORG-B that is currently absent.

Several related claims about the cause remain open or unverified: the carrier-flaky explanation (CL-02) is unverified and five related conflicts (C-1 through C-5) on the reject-cause assertion are still open.
output.summary: The requester (SH-REQ) originally asked for an AI agent to auto-fix and blanket-resubmit rejected shipment notices. Investigation using the carrier reject log (E-01: 3 records - 2x LOC_UNKNOWN, 1x EVENT_ORDER) showed the handoff itself (H-1) is healthy and valid, and the rejects trace to carrier-side business-rule checks on location/sequence data, not to generic fixable content errors or a flaky carrier system; this directly contradicted the requester's own framing (CL-01 CONTRADICTED, H-CONTENT-ERRORS REJECTED) and left the later 'carrier is flaky' claim (CL-02/E-02) unverified. The problem definition (PD-1) passed its DEFINE gate only CONDITIONALLY, deferring two high-criticality unknowns (sample representativeness and upstream-vs-carrier origin) as open verification obligations. Given this, only the diagnostic piece of the plan - confirming LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER as the reject drivers using DA-REJ - was actually released; the proposed fixes (pre-submission validation in ORG-A's process, and a cross-org reference-data sync with the carrier) were left unfinished because they are not feasible in the available time, require cross-org authorization that doesn't yet exist, and are blocked by the two open unknowns. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with nothing explicitly held back: the diagnostic result stands, but it is explicitly released alongside a documented set of limitations (small sample size, unresolved origin question, no reject-rate reduction yet, and blocked correction/resubmission) rather than claiming the underlying problem is fixed.
